title: Anthrobots recapitulate the bilateral symmetry of many wild-type species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anthrobots recapitulate the bilateral symmetry of many wild-type species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The link between straight-line movement and bilateral symmetry in Anthrobots suggests that these synthetic forms, self-assembling in a symmetrical environment, recapitulate a fundamental morphological property seen in many wild-type species and could be used to study how embryos establish a single body midplane.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This suggests that these synthetic forms recapitulate a fundamental morphological property observed in many wild‐type species.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis”. Scope: Anthrobots compared with bilaterally symmetric animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A restricted morphological similarity is measurable with comparative data. The stronger evolutionary and mechanistic implication is underdetermined by similarity alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare movement-axis symmetry metrics in Anthrobots with homologous metrics across public images or 3D models of bilaterian locomotors, testing a prespecified similarity threshold.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared bilateral symmetry does not establish a shared developmental mechanism.

Recapitulation and fundamental property lack a unique quantitative threshold.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.38
operationalizability: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data existence: 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Straight-line motion with mirror symmetry is a geometric description already covered by the symmetry measurements. Calling that pattern a recapitulation of animal bilateral organization, or a route into embryonic midplane formation, adds no observation that would distinguish it from ordinary mechanics of a ciliated spheroid. The statement is therefore not separable from its non-developmental reading.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Bilateral symmetry of a straight-swimming spheroid is measurable, but 'recapitulating a fundamental property of wild-type species' and usefulness for studying embryonic midplanes do not state a result that would come out differently if the symmetry were only a physical consequence of moving in a line.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any elongated swimmer looks bilaterally symmetric about its path.

No homology, shared gene circuit or shared midplane mechanism is specified that could fail while the shape similarity remained.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data existence: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.12
